data.title: Sanofi wins approval of venglustat for Gaucher disease
data.description:
• The US FDA approved Sanofi's (SNY) Infilbray (venglustat) for neurological manifestations of Type 3 Gaucher disease.
  • Approval was based on data from the phase 3 LEAP2MONO study that found venglustat led to improvements in neurological manifestations better than the enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) imiglucerase.
  • The drug's label carries warnings for suicidal ideation and behavior, lens opacification in pediatric patients, and embryofoetal toxicity.
  • Infilbray is an oral, glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor. Sanofi said it would pursue additional approvals for the treatment in other countries this year and in 2027.

data.title: Gold and silver sink to 14-month lows as hawkish Fed commentary boosts dollar
data.description:
Gold and silver futures fell Wednesday to their lowest levels since September 2025, pressured by a stronger dollar and expectations of further interest rate hikes before year-end by the U.S. Federal Reserve.

Gold dropped more than 3% and broke below $3,750/oz, while silver suffered even larger losses as concerns about industrial demand and tighter financial conditions compounded the selloff.

The release of hawkish minutes from the Fed's October meeting reinforced expectations for additional monetary tightening, indicating the central bank remains firmly committed to raising interest rates to bring inflation down to its 2% target.

The minutes echoed comments from ​Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller, who said the Fed needs to "shock people" as prices continue to rise more than he expected by either ⁠approving a 50-basis point rate hike in December or communicating a faster pace of rate increases in 2027.

The dollar strengthened to a fresh 19-month high on Wednesday, as the hawkish commentary and recent economic data solidified expectations for ​a rate hike next month.

"The selloff is being driven by hawkish Fed commentary pointing to the need for several additional rate hikes before spring to contain stubborn inflation, alongside continued dollar strength and real yields at multi-decade highs," Saxo Bank analysts said in a note.

Gold and silver are also getting dragged down in part by the slide in copper (HG1:COM), which plunged more than 5% on Comex to $5.6595/lb, its lowest settlement since April 7.

"Copper is getting hit hard, and the weakness is spilling across the complex," squeezed by worries about AI investment prospects, the Chinese demand outlook, and uncertainty around U.S. trade policy, Phil Flynn of Price Futures Group said.

"A firmer dollar and expectations that interest rates may stay higher are weighing on gold and silver, while momentum selling is adding pressure," Flynn added.

On Wednesday, front-month Comex gold (XAUUSD:CUR) for November delivery plunged 3.1% to $3,736.80/oz, and front-month Comex November silver (XAGUSD:CUR) slumped 4.8% to $44.999/oz, the lowest settlement for the respective metals since September 24 and 25, 2025.

data.title: Lockheed Martin wins five-year $316.6M deal for C-5 aircraft support
data.description:
• Lockheed Martin (LMT) announced on Wednesday that its Aeronautics division received a $316.6M U.S. Air Force IDIQ contract to support the C-5 Galaxy aircraft.
  • The contract covers supply chain management, repairs, engineering, and technical support.

  • The C-5 Contracting Branch is the contracting activity.

data.title: CAAP outlines $7.3B Argentina investment program as domestic passenger use fee moves to $9 on December 10
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Corporación América Airports (CAAP) Q3 2026

Management View

  • “The third quarter was marked by strong revenue growth, resilient international passenger demand and significant progress on the strategic front.” (CEO & Director Martin Francisco Eurnekian)
  • “Revenue growth was a clear highlight, increasing nearly 14%, well ahead of the low single-digit increase in passenger traffic.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian)
  • “Adjusted EBITDA remained broadly in line with last year despite continued pressure in Argentina from weaker domestic traffic, a challenging comparison base in our cargo business and higher peso-denominated operating costs.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian)
  • “Starting with tariffs. All passenger and aircraft fees are now denominated in U.S. dollars.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian) “The domestic passenger use fee will increase to $9 effective December 10, compared with an effective tariff of approximately $3.7 in the third quarter.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian)
  • “The agreement establishes a total investment program of approximately $7.3 billion over the remaining concession term.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian) “$6.7 billion will be funded through the existing trust structure, while $600 million will be invested directly by Aeropuertos Argentina.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian)
  • “The regulatory IRR was set at 14.3%, while maintaining our right to seek further contractual adjustments.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian)
  • “Total revenues increased 14%, once again outpacing traffic figures, supported by strong commercial revenue growth of 22%.” (CFO & Head of Business Development Jorge Arruda)
  • “Adjusted EBITDA, excluding IFRIC 12, totaled $192 million, declining 1% as continued growth across all our other markets was more than offset by headwinds in Argentina.” (CFO & Head of Business Development Arruda)

Outlook

  • “As discussed earlier, the increase in Argentina's domestic passenger use fee effective December 10 will also provide additional support to revenues going into 2027.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian)
  • “Scheduled runway maintenance at the Ezeiza Airport is expected to affect operations for 17 days during the fourth quarter.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian)
  • “Looking ahead, we remain encouraged by international traffic trends across our portfolio.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian)
  • Compared with last quarter’s messaging that “limited domestic airline capacity, planned runway maintenance and additional challenging comparison base for cargo revenues may continue to affect the country's near-term results,” management in Q3 emphasized observed domestic normalization: “We are also seeing a recovery in domestic traffic in Argentina despite the disruption caused by Flybondi's suspension of operations.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian)

Financial Results

  • “Consolidated revenue per passenger rose 12% to $22.7 from $20.2 in the same quarter last year.” (CFO & Head of Business Development Arruda)
  • “Total cost and expenses increased 21%.” (CFO & Head of Business Development Arruda) “Excluding the fuel business, total cost and expenses increased 10%.” (CFO & Head of Business Development Arruda)
  • “Cargo revenues… declined nearly 9%” due to “an extraordinarily tough year-on-year comparison base in Argentina.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian)
  • “Liquidity position… reached $840 million at the end of the quarter.” (CFO & Head of Business Development Arruda) “Cash used in financing activities primarily reflected the $148 million dividend paid to shareholders during the quarter… as well as debt repayments.” (CFO & Head of Business Development Arruda)
  • “Net leverage ratio remained at comfortable 0.7x.” (CFO & Head of Business Development Arruda) “After quarter end, our subsidiary, Aeropuertos Argentina, issued $400 million in 10-year notes with an 8% coupon.” (CFO & Head of Business Development Arruda)

Q&A

  • Alejandro Anibal Demichelis, Jefferies: Asked how much capacity can be added at Aeroparque and Ezeiza with the $600 million CapEx and how CAAP is thinking about Angola/Catania/Brazil opportunities. CFO Arruda: “The capacity of these terminals will go to, in the case of Aeroparque, 21 million and in the case of Ezeiza, 22 million passengers.” He added on deal flow: “We are making very good progress on Angola… Just today, we delivered a nonbinding offer to Catania in Sicily.”
  • Guilherme Mendes, JPMorgan: Asked whether Argentina’s contract changes and low leverage alter dividend policy, and requested Florence master plan milestones. CFO Arruda: “We will be running the same analysis… when we decided to pay the dividends of $150 million recently,” describing “4 main pillars,” and on Florence said, “we continue to make progress… we have nothing more… on a concrete basis to communicate.”
  • Sofia Vatta, Latin Securities: Asked if airline fuel pressures could impact CAAP airports. CFO Arruda: “So far, we have not seen any material impact in our operations in any part of the world because of the fuel costs.”
  • Pablo Ricalde Martinez, Itaú: Asked what CAAP expects for Armenia traffic growth in 2027 given new routes. CFO Arruda: “We expect more of the same, positive trends across all markets, except Middle East, which will continue under pressure given the geopolitical situation in the region.”
  • Daniel Vielman, BofA Securities: Asked for Argentina 2027 traffic outlook and how capacity returns post-Flybondi. CFO Arruda: “A significant portion of their traffic has already been replaced by… Aerolíneas and JetSmart,” and “Going forward, we see modest growth in the low single digits.”

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were neutral-to-slightly positive, concentrating on capital allocation (dividends), Argentina traffic normalization, and timing/visibility on growth projects; questions were framed as requests for “color” and “visibility” rather than challenges.
  • Management tone was slightly positive in prepared remarks and steady in Q&A, emphasizing milestones and discipline: “This amendment represents a major milestone for CAAP,” and on dividends, “our policy is… based on those 4 pillars.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian; CFO & Head of Business Development Arruda)
  • Versus Q2, management’s Q3 tone carried more conclusiveness on Argentina, moving from “once we have something that is binding” to detailing enacted terms such as “All passenger and aircraft fees are now denominated in U.S. dollars.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q3 introduced finalized Argentina concession economics and duration: “the amendment agreement entered into with the government of Argentina,” including “a material term extension” and a “concession extension of 18 years.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian) Q2 described an in-progress process: “we keep working with the regulator.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian)
  • Q3 also highlighted incremental strategic execution in Italy and Brazil: “we increased our indirect economic interest in Toscana Aeroporti… from approximately 62% to 68%,” and “we recently inaugurated the Partage shopping mall at Brasília Airport.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian) Q2 emphasized initiatives underway (Florence approvals; Montevideo commercial expansion) without these specific completions.
  • Analyst focus shifted from timing of renegotiations and recurring commercial revenue per passenger (Q2) toward capacity outcomes from the $600 million Argentina CapEx and capital returns under the new framework (Q3).

Risks and Concerns

  • “Domestic traffic remained affected by airline capacity constraints,” and Flybondi’s “total suspension… in early August” weighed on Argentina volumes. (CEO & Director Eurnekian)
  • “Scheduled runway maintenance at the Ezeiza Airport is expected to affect operations for 17 days during the fourth quarter.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian)
  • Cargo headwinds persisted from prior-year comparables: “an extraordinarily tough year-on-year comparison base in Argentina continued to weigh on total cargo revenues.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian) Management’s mitigation included “commercial and operational initiatives” and “2 new courier terminals at Ezeiza and Carrasco.” (CEO & Director Eurnekian)

Final Takeaway

CAAP management centered the quarter on a completed Argentina amendment that resets tariff currency to U.S. dollars, lifts the domestic passenger use fee to $9 on December 10, and embeds a roughly $7.3 billion investment program alongside a stated 14.3% regulatory IRR framework, while operationally pointing to international-led traffic growth, early signs of domestic recovery in Argentina after Flybondi’s suspension, and continued liquidity to fund both the $600 million Argentina direct investment commitment and external growth options such as Angola and the Catania process.

data.title: General Dynamics wins $332.5M Army contract for Stryker support
data.description:
• General Dynamics (GD) announced on Wednesday that its Land Systems business received a $332.5M U.S. Army IDIQ, a firm-fixed-price contract.
  • The contract covers maintenance and support services for its Stryker military vehicles.
  • It also covers equipment delivery, training, and field maintenance, with work expected to continue through November 17, 2031.
  • The work locations and funding will be determined with each order, while Army Contracting Command is the contracting activity.

data.title: Bankrupt Dish Wireless reaches $525M settlement with American Tower - report
data.description:
EchoStar (ECHO) subsidiary Dish Wireless has reached a $525M settlement with American Tower (AMT) and is in talks with other tower owners who say they're owed billions of dollars after its failed attempt to build a 5G network, according to a media report on Wednesday.

Dish is in the process of hammering out similar deals with other large creditors, including Charter Communications (CHTR),  which provided infrastructure and services for its 5G network, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing a court hearing.

Last year, EchoStar switched strategy and started selling spectrum licenses and winding down the 5G network operations after the Federal Communications Commission pressured Dish for taking too long to build the network.

The settlement funds are being paid from a $2.4B creditor trust established by the FCC using proceeds from AT&T's purchase of EchoStar's spectrum licenses. The settlement with American Tower will require FCC approval, the WSJ said.

Dish Wireless, the EchoStar unit that was building the 5G network, filed for Chapter 11 in June along with Dish DBS, another EchoStar subsidiary, so they could restructure their balance sheets.

data.title: Stocks to watch on Wednesday after hours: PANW, SNEX, MKL, YELP
data.description:
Wall Street's major averages finished mixed on Wednesday after Nvidia reported better-than-expected Q3 results amid the recent CEO scandal. The Nasdaq ended higher even as Nvidia closed lower.

The benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) finished -0.2%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) ended +0.4, and the blue-chip Dow (DJI) finished -1.1%.

Now, here are a few stocks to watch during extended trading hours:

  • Palo Alto Networks (PANW) surged 8% after releasing its first-quarter fiscal 2027 financial results, extending the stock's 9.9% surge logged in the regular trading session. The cybersecurity stalwart turned in adjusted earnings per share of $1.05 versus the $0.97 consensus estimate.
  • StoneX Group (SNEX) stock slid 2.9% as the company's fiscal Q4 earnings failed to meet Wall Street expectations. While operating revenue grew from a year ago but fell from fiscal Q3, its expenses rose both from the prior quarter and a year ago.
  • Markel Group (MKL) said that its board approved a $2.5B increase to its existing share repurchase authorization. Shares edged up 0.5%.
  • Yelp (YELP) disclosed a workforce reduction expected to affect nearly 5% of its full-time employees.

data.title: Borr Drilling reports 9M results
data.description: • Borr Drilling press release (BORR): Total operating revenues decreased by $19.0 million to $742.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $761.4 million for the same period in 2025. The decrease in total operating revenues is due to a decrease in dayrate revenue of $67.7 million, partially offset by an increase in bareboat charter revenue of $41.3 million and management contract revenue of $7.4 million.
